# Best travel chargers with multiple USB-C ports

**Top pick: UGREEN Nexode 100W 4-Port GaN charger**
- It has 3 USB-C ports and 1 USB-A port, and a foldable US plug.
- One of the top two USB-C ports can deliver the full 100W alone, which is enough for most laptops. With a laptop and a second device it splits to 65W and 30W. With all four ports in use it's 45W, 30W and 10.5W on the remaining ports.
- It's the heaviest of the picks at 8.3 oz, and no cable is included.
- Buy: use the "Check price on Amazon" button in [TechWise's GaN travel charger guide](https://www.techwisereviews.com/posts/best-gan-usb-c-chargers-travel-2026). It's also listed in [Android Central's USB-C charger guide](https://www.androidcentral.com/best-usb-c-phone-charger).
- One source ([VoyageHacks](https://voyagehacks.com/en/travel-gear/best-gan-wall-chargers-for-travel/)) describes it as four USB-C ports. Three others list three USB-C plus one USB-A, so check the listing's port layout before buying.

**Other options**
- **Smaller and lighter: Anker Prime 67W 3-Port.** It has 2 USB-C ports and 1 USB-A port, weighs 4.78 oz, and either USB-C port can output the full 67W alone. Two ports together cap at 65W. It suits a laptop, a phone and one accessory. [Buy via TechWise](https://www.techwisereviews.com/posts/best-gan-usb-c-chargers-travel-2026) or [VoyageHacks](https://voyagehacks.com/en/travel-gear/best-gan-wall-chargers-for-travel/).
- **Power-hungry laptop: Anker 737 GaNPrime 120W.** It has 2 USB-C ports and 1 USB-A port, with the most headroom of the three TechWise compared. [Buy via TechWise](https://www.techwisereviews.com/posts/best-usb-c-chargers-travel-multiple-devices-2026).
- **Built-in international plugs and several USB-C ports: Epicka TA-105 Max 75W.** It has 3 USB-C ports and 2 USB-A ports, with four switchable plug types, and Android Central calls it overpowered. It's a good fit if you'd rather not carry a separate plug adapter. [Buy via Android Central](https://www.androidcentral.com/accessories/power-charging/best-usb-adapter-for-travel).

**Before you buy**
- The headline wattage is shared across ports. Plug your laptop in first, then add the phone and smaller devices.
- The wall chargers above only have US prongs. Outside North America you need a plug-shape adapter, not a voltage converter, since they accept 100-240V.
- For 100W charging you need a 5A (100W-rated) USB-C cable. Plain cables can cap at 60W.

I can't open the product pages, so the links go to the reviews, which have the buy buttons. I can't confirm current prices.
